goal: Each team lead uses Claude to draft the weekly team report from the team's task tracker and checks every line against it before sending.

nodes.skill: Use Claude to draft the weekly team report from the task tracker and check every line against the tracker before sending it.
Ask Claude for a first draft and revise it until it says what you mean.
Have Claude draft the weekly report from a task-tracker export.
Check every line of a Claude draft against the tracker export and flag each line the export does not support before sending.
Start a conversation with Claude and send it a written request.

floor.detail: participant_profile.starting_level is 'New to Claude', so this cannot be assumed; anything below it (reaching Claude at all) depends on which Claude product and access participants have, which the inputs do not say.

nodes.skill: Write a request that tells Claude what to draft, who it is for and what it must contain.

floor.detail: participant_profile.learner: 'Team leads who already write the weekly report by hand', so they already know what the report must contain and who reads it.

data.what: Material Claude drafts the first practice draft from (weekly goal W1)

nodes.skill: Ask Claude to revise a draft by naming the specific changes you want.

floor.detail: participant_profile.learner: they already write the report by hand, so judging what to change in a draft is existing skill; the only new step is asking Claude, which rests on N6.

nodes.skill: Give Claude the tracker export to work from in the conversation.

floor.detail: Producing the export happens in the tracker, not with Claude, and the inputs do not say who produces it; splitting stops here.

data.what: The team's tracker export for the real report
data.quote: Tracker exports are read-only copies of real data; nothing is written back to the tracker.

data.what: The sample tracker file for practice reports
data.quote: Practice reports use the sample tracker file supplied by the presenter.

claims.text: Claude can take a file shared in a conversation as the material to work from.

nodes.skill: Ask Claude to draft the weekly report using only what the tracker export shows.

floor.detail: participant_profile.learner: they already write the weekly report, so they can state its content; the Claude steps it needs are already nodes N6 and N8, linked as prereqs.

claims.text: Claude can draft text that keeps to the contents of a file given in the conversation when asked to.

nodes.skill: Ask Claude to name, for each line of the draft, the tracker export row it comes from.

floor.detail: Asking for the source row of each line needs only the export already given to Claude (N8) and the draft (N9), both linked; nothing new comes before it.

claims.text: Claude can point to the rows of a file given in the conversation that a line of its draft is based on.

nodes.skill: Open the tracker export and confirm each line against the row Claude named, finding the row yourself where Claude named none.

floor.detail: Reading a row of a table and comparing it with a sentence is common knowledge; the tracker's status values it may need are an open gap (status code).

data.what: The team's tracker export the draft was made from
data.quote: Tracker exports are read-only copies of real data; nothing is written back to the tracker.

data.what: The sample tracker file when checking a practice report
data.quote: Practice reports use the sample tracker file supplied by the presenter.

nodes.skill: Flag each line the export does not support, note the row it was checked against, and ask Claude to correct or remove it.

floor.detail: participant_profile.learner: deciding a report line is wrong is existing report-writing skill; asking Claude to change it is N7, linked.

gaps.detail: Weekly goal W1 asks for a first draft, but the inputs do not say what Claude drafts it from (sample tracker file, the participant's own material, or something else).
The glossary marks it UNRESOLVED ('the tracker's status values are not yet listed'); reading export rows to draft (N9) and check lines (N11) depends on it.
Used in the constraints ('Tracker exports') and criteria, but not in the glossary: what an export contains and its form are not defined. 'sample tracker file' is likewise undefined.
The inputs do not say who produces the tracker export for a real report or how; producing it is outside Claude, so N8 stops at inputs_stop.
The inputs do not say which Claude product, plan or surface participants use, so the claims on N8, N9 and N10 are marked verify.

set_aside.reason: Delivery constraint (time and number of meetings); it does not shape capability.
